taxonomy.subtopic: Ectopic gastric mucosa and adjacent ileal ulceration

questions.stem_html:
A 6-year-old boy has recurrent episodes of painless maroon-colored stool. He is afebrile and has no abdominal tenderness. Hemoglobin is low. A technetium-99m pertechnetate scan shows a focus of uptake in the right lower abdomen that appears at the same time as the stomach.

Which process most directly causes the intestinal bleeding?

options.text_html: Pancreatic enzymes produced within the diverticulum digest a mesenteric artery
Failure of neural crest migration causes functional obstruction and mucosal ischemia
Persistent communication with the umbilicus permits bacterial invasion
Acid secretion by ectopic gastric mucosa ulcerates adjacent ileal mucosa
Intussusception always causes venous infarction before bleeding begins

questions.explanation_html: A Meckel diverticulum is a vitelline-duct remnant that may contain ectopic gastric mucosa. Acid damages nearby ileal mucosa, producing ulceration and painless bleeding; technetium is taken up by gastric mucosal cells. The simultaneous gastric and right-lower-quadrant uptake identifies ectopic gastric mucosa in a Meckel diverticulum.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Ectopic pancreatic tissue may occur, but acid-producing gastric mucosa is the classic cause of painless bleeding.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Neural crest failure causes Hirschsprung disease, not a technetium-avid diverticulum.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: A patent omphalomesenteric duct can drain at the umbilicus but is not required for painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Meckel can serve as a lead point, but this painless bleeding without obstruction is best explained by ectopic acid secretion.

questions.educational_objective: Explain painless pediatric lower gastrointestinal bleeding from a Meckel diverticulum through ectopic gastric acid secretion and adjacent ileal ulceration.
